sealed_record.thesis: The same TrendForce note gives two separate, independently sourced supply constraints that both point at WDC's core business: the DRAM shortage is now constraining NAND suppliers' ability to build enterprise SSDs, so eSSDs stay undersupplied through 2026, and on HDD, even with Toshiba's announced line expansion it takes 12-24 months to come online, so lead times do not improve before late 2027 at the earliest. Separately, China's YMTC - a NAND producer with every incentive to talk supply up - told The Wire China it expects the NAND shortage to last another three years. The market is still underwriting HDD as a structurally dying profit pool and NAND as a 2027 oversupply round-trip; both of those assumptions are contradicted by the people actually building the capacity. aleabitoreddit's point is the cleanest statement of the mispricing: an AI revenue headline does not end a multi-year physical capacity shortage, yet the whole complex trades on those headlines.
